summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with a history of CNS lymphoma was admitted for his scheduled six-month maintenance high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. He tolerated the infusion well without acute complications. His methotrexate level declined appropriately to 0.15, allowing for discharge with instructions to complete a three-day course of leucovorin and sodium bicarbonate, along with aggressive hydration. Hyponatremia (sodium 125–127) was noted and attributed to possible overuse of desmopressin for diabetes insipidus, though the patient remained asymptomatic and mentally clear. He expressed interest in extending his treatment interval to 12 months, but was advised to confirm the six-month schedule with his neuro-oncologist. All home medications were resumed, and outpatient follow-up with MRI was planned. He was discharged home in stable condition.
problems: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma, unspecified, extranodal and solid organ sites
